duzeltme.secenekler[1].text: Longer fatty acid chains have lower melting points, because longer chains are more flexible and cannot pack closely together.
duzeltme.secenekler[2].text: Double bonds raise the melting point, because they are stronger than single bonds and hold neighboring chains together more tightly.
duzeltme.secenekler[3].text: Melting point depends only on the number of carbon atoms in the chain, because each added carbon adds more contact between chains.
